newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bridgestone steps up overseas expansion.
newsitem.headline: Bridgestone steps up overseas expansion.

text.p: Japan's Bridgestone Corp is aggressively expanding its overseas business, boosting tyre output in markets including North America in a bid to achieve its goal of capturing 20 percent of the global tyre market.
The company is also considering widening its business to include potentially high-growth areas such as Russia, eastern Europe and China, where it has no production base yet.

Of the Bridgestone group's global tyre output of about 1.34 million tonnes in 1996, output in Japan hit a record high of 560,000 tonnes, while output from North America was 510,000 tonnes, the company said.
The company plans to spend $430 million in 1997 and 1998 to raise tyre production significantly in North America, where rival Goodyear Tyre & Rubber Co has a traditionally strong presence.

"In the North American market, where we have production facilities, we would like to shift to local production as soon as possible to meet demand from auto makers there," said Kenichi Kitawaki, Bridgestone's manager of public relations.
According to the U.S. trade magazine "Tire Business", Bridgestone's share in the world market on a value basis was about 18 percent in 1996, up from 14 percent in 1988.

Bridgestone's share of the North American market has steadily increased in recent years, rising to about 16 percent last year from about 11 percent in 1988, which may pose a threat to Goodyear. Goodyear's market share in the United States is estimated at about 30 percent.

Kitawaki said the company's favourable performance in the U.S. market was attributable to its restructuring efforts and the reform of its sales network in the United States, combined with its good performance in Indy Car racing.
"We tackled restructuring in our U.S. business earlier than our competitors," Kitawaki said.
Although the company has established itself as the market leader in Asia, French maker Michelin leads the European market, while Goodyear is strongest in the United States.
"First of all we aim to establish ourselves as the second largest maker in both the North American and the European tyre markets," Kitawaki said.
"Tyre demand in the U.S. still has growth potential," Kitawaki said, adding that more tough competition is expected.
One of the company's strategies to gain tyre market share around the world is to raise the profile of Bridgestone brands of tyres.
"By participating in the F1 (Formula One) race, we hope to make Bridgestone brand tyres more popular," Kitawaki said.
Bridgestone's investment plans for Russia, eastern Europe and China are still on the drawing board.

"In the markets where we have production facilities, we hope to raise local production. We need to expand into new growth areas for export purposes as the growth potential in Japan is limited," he said.
Of the domestic tyre output, about half is for exports.
